hardware_answers.question: Does Kismet's Data Sources panel (list_interfaces) show three rows per board (esp32c5-, esp32c5zigbee-, esp32c5btle-<tty>), hide all three rows of a board that is in use, and hide the entries named by mask_datasource_interface?

answers.answer: REST only, no browser. list_interfaces shows 3 rows per board (12 for 4 boards, plus hci0 and wlan0). All three rows of a board disappear when a C local, C remote or Python remote source holds it. The three mask_datasource_interface lines from Troubleshooting remove that board's three rows. The Data Sources panel itself was not looked at.
answers.evidence: n10: 14 -> 11 -> 5 rows; the masked run gave 11 rows without ttyACM3.

hardware_answers.question: Do both helpers behave the same for a board (names, UUID E5C5000M-...-<MAC> per radio, hardware label, channel= rules, port claims)? Does a by-id path give the MAC UUID in the Python helper? Is the board re-found by MAC on reopen, after a tty swap and after an unplug longer than 20 s?

answers.answer: Partial. The UUID per radio is identical across C local, C remote and Python remote (E5C5000M-0000-0000-0000-<MAC>, M=1/2/3), and so is the hardware label. A by-id path gives the MAC UUID in both helpers. A pty gets a path-hash UUID (E5C50001-...-C9B0E658C827). A local re-open after SIGKILL keeps the UUID. They differ in capture_interface (C 'esp32c5-<tty>', Python the path) and in the log shape: C '<name> capturing (wifi)', Python '<name> - /dev/ttyACM3 opened' / '... capturing'. tty swap, unplug and the Python 15 s give-up were not run.
answers.evidence: n1c, n8t, n9, n4r, n7, n15.

answers.answer:
Both helpers give a board the same identity: UUID E5C5000M-0000-0000-0000-<MAC> with M=1/2/3 for wifi/zigbee/btle, and the same hardware label. The Python helper gives the MAC UUID for a ttyACM name, a by-id link and a /tmp symlink alike.

The same board twice in one process is refused. After the 15 s give-up (download-mode trick), the source reconnects under the same UUID.

The tty swap and a true unplug over 20 s were not tested; they need a physical replug.

hardware_answers.question: Can the Pi rows be marked as re-run with the final C helper, the Python helper on the Pi and the current firmware? This includes flashing a board as Flashing-the-Firmware says and then capturing.

answers.answer: Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.
answers.evidence: Coverage of the other checks in this session: p2-p21.

hardware_answers.question: Does a board on the sibling's 1.2.0 web-flasher image sync and capture Wi-Fi, zigbee and btle under both final helpers? What are the BTLE fix-up behaviour and message text, and the length checks (no false drops)?

answers.answer: Yes, on the Kismet side (the extcap part, id 130, was not run). Board D8:0C on the published 1.2.0 image synced and captured all three radios under the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers. Wi-Fi: 792 / 516 / 342 packets. Zigbee: 200/200 TXTEST frames each, link type 230. BTLE: 2536 / 1141 / 633 packets, with 13/12/12 devices. The board sends flags 0x0013 and a zero CRC. Every helper rewrites each record to 0x0C13 with a valid CRC (100% of 4,323 pcapng packets checked) and logs this once per helper connection, verbatim: '<name>: the board's firmware does not mark BTLE packets as CRC checked, so Kismet would drop them; the helper fills in the CRC and the flags (the board only reports packets whose CRC passed). Flashing current firmware makes this unnecessary'. In Kismet it reads 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a local source and 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a remote one. There were 0 'impossible length' drops and 0 error packets. The only differences from current firmware are the fix-up message and the 0x0013 flags on the wire.
answers.evidence: f10w.out, f10z.out, f10b.out, f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10raw.json
